Algebraic connectivity λ2 is concave in individual nonnegative edge conductances, so averaging over S_m×S_{p−1} preserves weighted cost and cannot worsen λ2; one two-class allocation attains the unrestricted global value, without claiming all asymmetric optima symmetric. Reconstructed full spectrum: S=a+(p−1)b, mb and two nonzero quotient roots with quadratic λ²−[(m+1)a+(m+p−1)b]λ+m(m+p)ab. Unit-gap feasibility b≥1/m and a≥max{1−(p−1)b, g(b)} where g(b)=((m+p−1)b−1)/(m(m+p)b−(m+1)). g' =−(p−1)/d², g''>0, intersection at b=β=(m+2(p−1)+sqrt(m²−4(p−1)))/(2(p−1)(m+p)). Boundary expense slope switches at r=P/Q=1; on convex branch it switches at r=R=d(β)², generating all three specified C_* and (a,b) formulas. Verified the quadratic trace/root condition excludes double-subunit-root cases. λ2^*=B/C_* and R~m^4/(p−1)^2. Independent full Laplacian eigenvalues and numerical optimizations checked 24 parameter/price cases, but general result is analytic.
